editorNote: The first week of 1983 keeps the personal computer on the newsstand: TIME makes the machine the symbol of 1982 while stores sell budget BASIC machines, cartridges, and IBM PC software to new owners.
morningLine: The new year opens with computers on magazine covers, cartridges in living rooms, and shoppers learning the price difference between starter micros and office PCs.

lead.headline: Machine of the Year Sends Home Computers Into 1983
lead.summary: TIME’s Jan. 3 issue names the computer its Machine of the Year, turning 1982’s surge of home micros, IBM PCs, school machines, and game cartridges into a mainstream newsstand story for the first shopping week of 1983.
lead.confidence: High for TIME issue date and framing; retail emphasis is week-context from period hardware and game-market sources.

computerItems.title: TIME puts the computer where Person of the Year used to stand
computerItems.summary: The Jan. 3, 1983 issue treats the computer as the defining force of 1982, emphasizing its spread through homes, schools, and offices.

computerItems.title: Starter machines make BASIC a counter-top promise
computerItems.summary: Timex Sinclair 1000, VIC-20, and Commodore 64 price points show how stores can sell programming and games to first-time families at very different budgets.

computerItems.title: Atari warning chills the game boom’s new year

computerItems.confidence: Medium; January trade reporting ties the warning to late-1982 events.
